_about: 问签 v1 (Hanli 2026-11-02: 「可以, 按你说的做」 — the rewards, then the v1 scope; rules/fortune.mjs, rules/almanac.mjs, guide/qian.md, doc/design.md § 问签). One 签 a real day from the 签筒, seeded by the day and the save. `qian`: the traditional 观音灵签, all one hundred, each 签诗 and grade quoted exactly from the temple's own page (`source`, and each 签's `url`; typos kept as published, e.g. 签20's 开睛); `gloss` is the game's plain English rendering, not a translation of record (no faithful public-domain English translation was found). `grades`: the 签's grade as the source states it, and the day's 修为 `speed` it gives (上上 ×1.2, stepping down to ×1.0 at 中 and below — never under 1: a bad draw takes nothing). `yi`: the one kind of play the 签 names 宜 today (`kinds[(n − 1) mod 4]`), whose 修为 pays ×`pay` today; `weight` is what the 时辰 pool may lean a game of that kind by (fortune.mjs yiWeightOf). A kind matches a grant by its system's tag (`plays`), else a board's mechanic (`mechanics`), else its table (`tables`). `asks`: what he may ask about (optional). `streak`: 连签 — days in a row draw a finer 签筒. `yingyan`: 应验 — from `after_hour` 银月 may ask once whether the 宜 came true; an answer pays `pay` (the small `game` table) and is kept in the save. `signs`: the twelve 星座 by month·day (MMDD, from · to). `almanac`: the 黄历 tables (rules/almanac.mjs).

almanac._about: 黄历 of the day, deterministic (rules/almanac.mjs): 日柱 from the Julian Day (1949-10-01 甲子); 月建 by the 节 (立春 opens 寅, the 节 day the new month's); 年 at 立春; 建除 — 建 the day whose branch is the month's (《欽定協紀辨方書》卷四: 「其法從月建上起建，與斗勺所指相應，如正月建寅，則寅日起建，順行十二辰是也」; 「每月交節，則疊兩值日」), after 《淮南子·天文訓》 「寅為建，卯為除，辰為滿，巳為平，午為定，未為執，申為破，酉為危，戌為成，亥為收，子為開，丑為閉」; 冲 the opposite branch; 煞 the day's 三煞 (申子辰 南 · 寅午戌 北 · 亥卯未 西 · 巳酉丑 东). Each officer's 宜 · 忌 are read from the gods 《協紀辨方書》卷四 sets on it (`from`, quoted), https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/欽定協紀辨方書_(四庫全書本)/卷04 — these are the 建除 宜忌 alone; a printed almanac's full list adds many other 神煞 and is longer. Checked against published almanacs (tests/qian.test.mjs): 2025-11-06 己卯 执, 2025-11-08 辛巳 破 冲猪 煞东, 2025-11-20 癸巳 破, 2025-11-30 癸卯 定 (skillon.com Tong Shu 2025-11, the 丁亥 month from 11-07); 2025-11-07 庚辰 冲狗 煞南 (qmrl888 · tianqi 老黄历); 2026-11-02 丙午年 戊戌月 庚辰日 (wannianli.tianqi.com). On a 节 day itself, sites that turn the month at the 节's hour (skillon: 2025-11-07 破) differ from this day-level rule (执 — the 協紀辨方書's 疊兩值日).

officers.from: 建日吉多可用；小時：其日忌結姻親開倉庫
吉期：所值之日宜出軍行師攻城寨興弔伐㑹親姻；除為四利太陽小吉
福德：其日宜祀神祗求福願修宫室；天巫：宜合藥請醫；天狗：其日忌禱祀鬼神祈求福願
天罡 · 河魁：所值之日百事宜避；死神：其日忌請醫服藥出師征討種植樹木進人納畜
時隂：所值之日宜運謀算畫計䇿睦子孫㑹親友；官符：其日忌拜官視事上表章陳詞訟；死氣：其日忌戰鬬征伐療病求醫……經營栽植
枝德：其日宜修造築垣；小耗：其日忌經營種蒔納財交易開市
大耗：其日忌營庫藏出財物逺經求取債負
危為極富星為谷將星為四利龍德吉
天醫：其日宜請藥避病尋巫禱祀
時陽：所值之日宜叙婚姻行宴樂；生氣：其日宜修築城壘開道溝渠起土修營養育羣畜種蒔

qian.gloss: Heaven and earth begin a good match; the day is right and all is whole. An upright heart is called to honour.
The carp still keeps to the river and cannot rise yet; one day it changes and leaps the Dragon Gate.
Home through wind and rain like a swallow: it carries mud to build its nest, and the nest crumbles, and it carries mud again.
An old mirror made whole again: broken bonds mend, the house is renewed, and good fortune passes to the children.
An awl digging for a spring: hard work finds little, but by chance a true friend appears and you rise together.
Sheltering under the cliff like a nesting bird, one must stand up as a grown man; schemes alone carry no one far.
Rushing on, blocked again and again, through mud and over mountains; looking for work far away, the road home is long.
Pines and cypresses stand strong; snow and frost do them no harm. One day they become the beams of a great hall.
Do nothing for selfish ends; speak it openly. A clear heart shines like the moon at the height of the sky.
Treasure lies hidden at home while you search far away — like carrying a lamp to look for fire. Stop and look nearer.
Great things can be done, though family matters keep you busy; in the end a patron shows the way.
Bad turns to good in a moment; a worthy friend comes down the mountain. Good news comes in the years of the tiger and the hare.
Born in a rich house, surrounded by fine things, given a purple-and-gold sash: a good name across the land.
Like a crane let out of its cage: every road opens, nothing blocks you, straight up to the ninth heaven.
The traveller fumes at the day; when trouble comes, stay back. The nest is broken — find a quiet, deep place to rest.
The furrowed brow eases; joy comes out of the clouds. Jade hidden in the dirt is found by a good craftsman.
Do not listen to idle talk of right and wrong; keep a quiet mind. Taking wild words as true is like eating a painted cake.
The sun sets, the moon rises, round and round since ancient times: whoever you are, things go your way.
Steering a boat home over the rapids, with wind and waves rising: to be safe, wait for calm water before you cross.
After long spring rain the sky clears; sun and moon grow bright. Old troubles fade, new things go well — a leap past the Dragon Gate.
Yin and yang meet as heaven wills: a happy marriage, dragon and snake together, a family made whole.
In the drought the fields are parched; then sweet rain pours. Everything grows green — one rain is worth a thousand gold.
Reaching for the laurel in the moon palace, why fear heaven's gate is shut? Good news comes, and everyone laughs.
No reason, no home; a fickle heart like a falling flower. Ask for favour and you will need effort; in the end things are tangled.
Past several worries and dangers, from now on you stand firm. A calm mind finds its own way; a wise person helps you to great things.
Word passes up and down and turns to nothing; a letter from far away promises success, yet to the end it is empty.
Each plan, each chance, weighed back and forth, never dared. When the time comes a patron helps, and you stand as firm as a mountain.
The moon rises in the east, lovely; clouds cover it for a while. It waxes and wanes — and talk against it is only talk.
A sword in its sheath gathers no dust; drawn out by a patron, it shines, and everyone respects it.
Do not go asking others for help: like a crane flying into a hidden arrow, like a snake in the grass when you gather firewood.
Sit in peace with nothing to worry about; eat when hungry, sleep when tired. Let go and no wrong or harm will come.
The way ahead is dim but sure: jade hides inside the stone, and when a good craftsman cuts it open, all is well.
You hold priceless treasure within; why look outside? Wait for someone who knows its worth, and keep your heart easy.
Courteous in going and coming, true in word and deed; if the heart is unclear, be still — the red sun stands at noon.
Put the family's old ways back in order; what looks like no merit is merit. Clear the thorns from the road; three agree as one.
Illness and lawsuits need no worry; there is wealth to be sought. Like a monkey freed from its chain, back home to its cave.
Wait for peace and better luck; a candle in the wind is no good. Better sit quietly inside, where the light stays steady.
Moonlight on a quiet house, suddenly lost in cloud and mist. Keep faith and the clouds will part; then is the time to act.
News from far away is hard to read; do not hope too hard. Grinding a stone into a mirror is wasted work.
The sun sets, the moon rises; yin grows and all goes well. For a woman especially: wealth and blessing increase.
Remember these good words: do not take a thief for your son. Do not crave a little sweetness now and suffer later.
The ruler's grace returns; pray and blessings grow. Everyone shares in it, in heaven and on earth.
Heaven and earth turn and all things are whole; you keep and care for yourself in peace. Everything goes as you wish.
Evenly matched at the board, black and white still undecided: one move decides it, so think it through.
Gentleness has always beaten force; a house that does good prospers. Like finding sweet drink when you are thirsty.
Keep to your old work patiently, keep your heart steady and do no wrong; when help comes, the old tree flowers again.
Flowers on brocade, the colours brighter still; luck brings rank and wealth together. Late success is still success, known far and wide.
In autumn the small bird becomes the great roc and soars ten thousand miles, where no other bird can follow.
Heaven is cold, the earth frozen, the water turned to ice: do not chase fame now. Keep still; the time will change.
Sail the five lakes and four seas, sails high; with a fair wind you arrive, the boat full of treasure.
The long hot summer day, everyone sweltering; heaven understands, and a cool breeze comes by itself.
Fishing the moon out of the water: all that effort and nothing caught. Say nothing idle; do not wear yourself out alone.
Disappointment turns to success; dragon and tiger call together. The blue sky has its road; success will come.
Treasure found in a dream, gone on waking — an empty dream. For marriage or illness, look for another way.
A good father passes it down to his sons and grandsons; enough food and clothing; parents happy; eat, drink and sleep in peace.
The stream sounds over small stones; the breeze and the moon keep the great busy. Ask the way, and leave the flowers in the wood alone.
Gossip is wind past the ear; good clothes and fortune come by themselves. Forget the old grudges: you and I think alike.
Remember plain words: do not seek a new trade far away. Keep to your old work; anything else will not go well.
Hiding high in a tower ringed with thorns; how long one lives is heaven's. Gain one, lose two.
Fighting fire with firewood only spreads the blaze. For honour or for going out, better to put it away and stop.
Poems at sunset, songs under the moon, laughing along with it all; what is met cannot be hidden, and all sing together.
Morning and evening the Buddha holds you up; danger comes and is not danger. When a patron leads you, wealth follows.
The needle lost at sea from a boat long ago, searched for again today: even if you find it, it costs time and heart.
A fish in a green pool runs into a net on every side; it finds no way out, and trouble follows.
Joy now is not yet joy; neither danger nor peace. Cutting flesh to patch a sore is no help — keep to the old and wait.
The road is steep, the horse tired, the traveller hurried; soldiers cut off; the boat broken by waves; flowers fade in the frost.
A golden thread weighs your heart: nothing more, nothing less. Upright all your life, your learning and skill shine.
Joy at the gate; a house that does good prospers. Marriage, fields and silkworms all go well; illness meets its cure.
A plum branch on the winter ridge: leaves fall, the branch is bare, but it never breaks. When spring comes it flowers first.
Every day like a bee among flowers, flying south-west, then east; when spring ends there is nothing to find, yet it keeps its old path.
The green dragon comes down to the road; one bow, two arrows; riding the dragon, you settle in peace.
To keep bees for honey, beware the sting; there may be another road ahead, but it is dark and thorny.
Spring thunder wakes the insects; turning over, out of the mud; going out and coming back, one day it becomes a dragon.
Like a swan flying into a cage: it tries to turn but cannot get out, north, south, east or west.
Like carrying a tiger over a high mountain, trembling with fear; luckily a skilled hand ahead keeps you safe.
Fish and dragon mixed together; wait in the deep pool for luck to turn. One morning you rise and leap the Dragon Gate.
Riches talked of in a dream; fame beyond the clouds is empty; far roads, hard to trust — until a patron points the way and you smile.
Cold water not yet boiled: neither cold nor hot, just warm. Travel anywhere and no harm comes, for you have many skills.
A vow made for peace: the peace was kept but the vow not yet repaid. Do not forget to repay it; do not take the gods' word lightly.
Climbing the immortals' cliff to learn the way, one day you are called to court. Sun and moon shine; an upright heart is known far and wide.
Plane leaves fall as autumn ends; the traveller hurries home like a cloud. Thanks to heaven, a fair wind brings the boat home full of treasure.
Flames fill the sky, and in the fire a lotus grows. In the end no harm is done; the leaves grow and the root holds.
Like the moon on the third, fourth and fifth nights, half there, not yet full: wait for the fifteenth, and it shines everywhere.
Losing virtue for a name, what is the use? Luck may turn to trouble. Drunk, not knowing where you are going, dreaming under the pines.
Clouds and fog hide the mountain road; spring ends, flowers fall and bloom again. Wake from the dream through study, and a patron leads you up.
Spring flowers light the terrace; carts come from afar with treasure. Like leaping the Dragon Gate's three waves — thunder on flat ground.
Halfway up the ridge with the sun on the hills, the cliffs not safe yet; look to heaven for protection, and you are still at peace.
A tiger of wood stands at the gate: it looks fierce but harms no one. It is plainly nothing to fear, yet worry keeps you uneasy.
Going out and making plans: great luck. Flawless jade hidden in the stone; when a patron guides you, you find the treasure and shine.
Word flies up to heaven; the boat comes home full of treasure. Ask about the road: it goes well, and there is still help ahead.
Lift your brows and step forward; the way ahead changes, with joy and wealth. A road as wide as the sky; whatever you give comes back.
A trader since youth, full of plans, with wealth that comes unasked. If you seek advancement: the scholar goes out and comes back first in the land.
The phoenix's feathers weighed down by rain, mocked by sparrows; one day the sky clears and it spreads its wings again.
A gentleman does not act like a petty man; a slip brings trouble. A zither needs a friend who knows its music; keep steady and calm.
Your will and work grow day by day, but wine and pleasure are too much. When the golden rooster calls, wealth and blessing come.
A great pagoda, out of the ordinary, shining on all eight sides: set your heart on doing good, and heaven sends blessing.
A candle in the wind casts empty shadows, like flowers in a mirror; the children come again and again to gather them, and gather nothing.
Plans for going out should wait; hurry brings worry and trouble. Like a bird flown into a net — how long until it gets free?
Riding straight in with whip in hand: half worry, half trouble, like a house burned down — and then heaven's rain washes the ashes away.
The gods are clear to you; a foolish person only grows more confused. The old man takes his stick and goes: better to keep to the old ways and wait.
